scope: Read-only stdlib full-EOS binary readout saturation/quality distinction using only existing saved native64 and original186 responses. Saved single-probe rows are excluded. No new model/FLA/DT/backward/optimizer calls, no production change or proposed scaling.

formula.secant_scope: Descriptive path-averaged binary log-prob derivative, not a correction factor, accuracy target, alternative reward or new tolerance. Mean |d| / mean |delta margin| measures saturation of the stated readout target relative to its own margin; it is not a fraction of the PG loss gap.

native64_full_EOS.actual_geometry_scope: Each case actual4 variants; use original row0 fact,row1 fullEOS only; actual FP32 categorical log_probs both labels saved. Derived margin from both stored LPs cancels their common normalizer; original native logits not persisted. Native-v2 layout is different from the formal paired-attribute layout.

original_formal186.geometry_scope: Original paired B4/8 c7fc runner endpoints,192 transport rows de-duplicated by first occurrence of actual UID/env_step to186responses from21successful trajectories. Only target1 LP is saved. Other class LP and margin are inferred from the declared binary normalizer using log(1-exp(LP1)); do not call these saved raw logits.

UID_balanced.scope: Compute each UID descriptive mean/secant ratio first, then equally average21UIDs; responses within a UID are correlated.

joint_vector_allocation_observation.scope: Actual saved full186 response vectors, not a measurement of all-token deletion accuracy. No explicit target/source-length average exists in owner source.
joint_vector_allocation_observation.meaning: Small average individual coefficients coexist with appreciable full-response effects and larger summed absolute vector mass. This describes allocation across many token entries plus signs; it does not prove literal divide-by-length, identify a model-forecast error, or determine how much of PG weakness is an attribution error.

interpretation_boundaries.label_bias: All64 use the same fixed0/1 mapping and one query. EOS predicts success for all64 under argmax and high p1; compatible with a positive class prior, but label lexical preference and an optimistic task forecast are not identifiable separately without independent/mapping-controlled evidence. Variation by goal/content means outputs are not constant; it does not exclude label bias.
interpretation_boundaries.forecast_quality: Actual64 first-response forecasts are high relative to this realized batch and weakly distinguish success/failure;4of8prompt groups have lower mean forecast on successful than failed trajectories. This is batch-level forecasting evidence, not a population calibration theorem and not a specific formatting defect.
interpretation_boundaries.saturation: The original186 success-target |d|/|delta margin| secant is about0.243. Thus the stated log-p1 readout is less responsive than its margin when p1 is high, as its correct formula requires. There is no basis to replace it with margin, unsaturate credit, or attribute the full1/211 gradient gap to this factor.
interpretation_boundaries.joint_credit: Full-response endpoint signals are not uniformly zero; no extra length division is found. Existing vector statistics are compatible with credit distributed across many tokens and signed cancellation. They do not distinguish correct small token effects from inaccurate joint conditional allocation on the full population.
interpretation_boundaries.next_repair_claim: This audit establishes no warranted template/label/scaling repair. Fixed Q/V/A, original categorical target, entropy and official actor remain unchanged; previously observed single-token differences are supplementary and do not identify full-batch error share.
